EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT CLINICAL NOTE
Date of visit:
The patient had recently returned from visiting family in the UK and resumed outdoor masonry work for Desert Line Construction in July.
segments.orig: The patient had recently returned from visiting family in the UK and resumed outdoor masonry work for Desert Line Construction in July.

segments.t: The patient presents with fever, weakness, nausea, and rapidly worsening confusion. Temperature is 40.0°C, pulse 123/min, blood pressure 100/61 mmHg, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. The patient is drowsy but arousable and has diffuse abdominal discomfort without peritoneal signs. There is no cough, dysuria, neck stiffness, or focal deficit. Skin is hot and flushed with limited perspiration. Sodium is 151 mmol/L, creatinine 1.9 mg/dL, lactate 4.4 mmol/L, AST 171 U/L, and creatine kinase 1,020 U/L. White-cell count is 14.2 ×10⁹/L; chest radiograph and urinalysis are negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Working diagnosis withheld for review. Admit / treat per protocol; senior review requested.
Attending:

data.weakest_point: The combination of exact age, sex, nationality, employer, occupation, and municipality—especially the rare employer–occupation pair—makes each note highly linkable even though direct identifiers are redacted.
strategies: Rare demographic and occupational profile scoring

data.findings: Extreme hyperthermia after resuming outdoor work, rapidly worsening confusion, hot flushed skin with reduced sweating, dehydration/hypernatremia, acute kidney injury, lactic acidosis, transaminitis, and elevated creatine kinase strongly support heat stroke, with systemic inflammatory shock physiology and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms as secondary considerations.
